title: FAST: An FHE Accelerator for Scalable-parallelism with Tunable-bit
problem: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) imposes enormous computational overhead compared to plaintext computation, and existing FHE accelerators do not exploit recent cryptographic optimizations—specifically hoisting technology and the gadget decomposition key-switching (KLSS) method—leaving significant performance on the table. Additionally, ciphertext level consumption varies significantly during application execution, causing workload imbalance that accelerators with fixed precision do not address.
motivation: FHE enables direct computation on encrypted cloud data, but its performance gap vs. plaintext computation makes real-world adoption infeasible without hardware acceleration that co-optimizes cryptographic algorithm improvements and variable precision requirements across the computation.
method: FAST is a hardware accelerator for Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE—computing on encrypted data without decrypting it). It implements two cryptographic optimizations: hoisting (which eliminates redundant number-transformation operations during key-switching) and KLSS gadget decomposition key-switching (an efficient method for processing encryption keys). The accelerator dynamically switches between these methods during execution based on how computationally complex the encrypted data is, using tunable-bit arithmetic (adjustable calculation precision) to match each method's specific requirements. It scales by configuring its array of processing elements to handle varying workload demands.
key_novelty: FAST is one FHE accelerator supporting hoisting and both hybrid and KLSS gadget-decomposition key-switching, dynamically switching between methods as the ciphertext level changes (encrypted data's computational complexity) and adjusting calculation precision accordingly.
contributions: Integration of hoisting technology and KLSS key-switching method into a hardware FHE accelerator, exploiting recent cryptographic optimizations not previously hardware-supported.
A versatile dual-method framework supporting both hybrid and KLSS key-switching in one accelerator, with dynamic selection based on ciphertext level.
Tunable-bit arithmetic datapath that adapts computational precision to the requirements of each key-switching method and ciphertext level.
Scalable parallel architecture (FAST) demonstrating improved FHE application throughput over prior accelerators.
